content:
maria_support: FYI - customer Acme Corp (cust_987) opened an urgent request: they have a court order and want us to pause automatic deletions for their tenant for 45 days. They claim a deletion run started yesterday at ~10:12 UTC. KMS key referenced: projects/redwood/keys/acme-kms. Can we confirm what actually ran and whether we can stop/restore anything?

ana_prodops: tagging @sam_security and @elena_legal. We need legal guidance first on holding data. From ops side, next steps are to confirm whether the deletion job completed and whether snapshots/backups exist.

sam_security: Acknowledged. Quick checklist: (1) confirm delete job id(s) and status in retention-cleaner, (2) check audit logs for delete API invocations and who/what triggered them, (3) check KMS/HSM decrypt errors around that time. If the KMS key was disabled, API might have failed with 403 vs completed deletions.

jon_engineering: I can look up the retention-cleaner runs. Deploy bot shows scheduled runs. Can someone paste the exact time from their ticket?

maria_support: Ticket shows customer-reported window 2026-11-12 10:12:09 UTC. They say they clicked "Apply TTL 30d" earlier and then requested a hold yesterday, but unsure of timings.

deploy-bot: retention-cleaner v2 executed at 2026-11-12T10:12:05Z job_id=rc-20261112-101205 status=IN_PROGRESS

jon_engineering: Found related job in internal queue: rc-20261112-101205. Logs show object deletions queued. I'll tail the cleaner logs for final status.

jon_engineering: log snippet:
```
[2026-11-12T10:12:05Z] rc-20261112-101205 start
[2026-11-12T10:12:29Z] deleting object id=s3://redwood-backups/cust_987/obj_4532
[2026-11-12T10:12:34Z] deletion succeeded object=obj_4532
[2026-11-12T10:12:41Z] deleting object id=s3://redwood-backups/cust_987/obj_4533
[2026-11-12T10:12:44Z] KMS decrypt error key=projects/redwood/keys/acme-kms err=ACCESS_DENIED
[2026-11-12T10:12:44Z] deletion skipped object=obj_4533
[2026-11-12T10:12:50Z] rc-20261112-101205 finished summary: attempted=24 deleted=20 skipped=4
```

sam_security: The KMS decrypt error is important. If decrypt failed for some objects, those wouldn't have been deleted. But others succeeded. We need to enumerate which objects were deleted vs skipped. Also check HSM audit for any admin key disables around 10:10-10:13 UTC.

maria_support: Customer is asking if we can restore the 20 deleted objects or recover ordered data. They explicitly wrote it's part of discovery.

elena_legal: Per legal, if deletion already completed we can only provide a record of actions and check backups. We must not attempt to alter custody until legal confirms preservation scope. Please collect an evidence bundle: audit log exports, retention-cleaner job logs, KMS audit entries, and list of object ids deleted/skipped.

ana_prodops: Repro steps for ops to fetch data:
1) export audit logs for protoPayload.methodName=DeleteObject for customer cust_987 between 2026-11-12T10:00Z and 2026-11-12T11:00Z
2) query internal job store: SELECT object_id, status FROM retention_deletes WHERE job_id='rc-20261112-101205'
3) check S3 lifecycle and snapshots: aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket redwood-backups --prefix cust_987/
4) check KMS HSM audit: hsm-audit query --key acme-kms --from 2026-11-12T10:00Z --to 2026-11-12T10:20Z

sam_security: Additional commands to get the delete API call payload (useful to see who triggered):
```
# internal logging query
gcloud logging read "resource.type=cloud_run_revision AND protoPayload.methodName=DeleteObject AND jsonPayload.customerId=cust_987" --limit 50 --format=json
# or internal elastic query
ES: GET /audit-logs/_search {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"match":{"customer.id":"cust_987"}},{"match":{"event":"object.delete"}}]}}}
```

jon_engineering: I pulled the job table: we have a CSV of all attempted deletions. I'll attach to the case. Deleted objects list count=20, skipped count=4. Skipped objects had KMS errors.

maria_support: Customer asked whether we can temporarily flip their retention policy to 'hold' to prevent any future deletes while legal evaluates. Is that something we can apply immediately?

sam_security: We have an internal per-tenant hold flag (internal_only.preserve_until). We can set preserve_until = 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z for cust_987, but we need legal sign-off. Once set, retention-cleaner will skip that tenant on next runs.

elena_legal: Authorizing a temporary hold pending subpoena review. Legal requests: (a) preserve_until = 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z, (b) gather evidence bundle and lock chain-of-custody, (c) create internal incident CR-2026-112-A.

ana_prodops: I'll run the patch to set the hold flag now (internal API). Command:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://internal.redwood/v1/tenants/cust_987/hold -d '{"preserve_until":"2027-01-01T00:00:00Z","reason":"legal_subpoena"}'
```

deploy-bot: API request accepted: hold-set job hs-20261112-0001 status=SUCCESS

sam_security: Next: we should export KMS audit logs and HSM entries to the evidence bundle. Also collect key policy snapshots. I'll coordinate with infra.

jon_engineering: Quick note — for the deleted objects we might still have snapshot copies in cold backups (s3-glacier) depending on retention. If legal requests recovery, recovery windows and costs vary. Ops: enumerate backup tiers and earliest possible restore ETA.

maria_support: Customer informed that we have set the hold and legal is engaged. They want a timeline for evidence and whether any data can be restored. I told them we will follow up in 2 hours with a status update.

elena_legal: Confirming incident CR-2026-112-A created and assigned to @sam_security and @jon_engineering. Legal will provide subpoena copy offline.

sam_security: Will share evidence bundle once exports complete. If backups contain deleted data, recovery is a manual process and may take 24-72 hours depending on tier.

maria_support: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source. Will update customer in 2 hours. :thumbsup:
